title: Nine Hundred Pages of Reading
subtitle: 经典与名著 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经典与名著（文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）
meta: 主题语境：经典与名著（文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）　|　核心词汇：classic　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 classic 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 my mother was sent to read ① classic she could not finish, and she said the reading was the whole of the lesson. The ② classic, meaning the book and not the style, was nine hundred pages long and was read by whoever came last; classic, she said, is the only thing on a shelf that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ classic on that shelf had the same preface, and the ④ classic at the end, meaning the one the teacher kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever read properly. Classic, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ classic was the whole of the exam, meaning the standard it carried and not the book. The ⑥ classic, meaning the standard and not any of that, is the only thing in an exam that everybody cites and nobody questions; classic, he said, is either something you read or the only word that means both a book and a standard. She said the standard is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ classic had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the preface. The ⑧ classic of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine hundred pages and eleven years of reading; classic, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ classic I remember is the one at the end, which was read in 1976 and is still described as the shortest in the county. A ⑩ classic, my grandmother said in 1981, is the only thing that improves by being read; every classic, she said, is a standard that has agreed to look like a book. She said the standard was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 经典作品；名著
B. n. 名著（指那本书本身，与那种风格相对）
C. 固定搭配：read a classic 读一部经典
D. n. 名著（指那个书架上每一部）
E. n. 名著（指末尾那一部）
F. n. 典范（抽象：它承载的那条标准）
G. n. 那条标准（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The classic, meaning the book and not the style
classic was the whole of the exam
the classic had become a number in a report
The classic of the whole thing
A classic, my grandmother said in 1981

answers.why: read a classic 意为“读一部经典”，1956 年母亲被派去读她读不完的那部经典。
classic 意为“经典作品、名著”，指那本书本身而不是那种风格，共九百页，由最后来的人读。
classic 指那个书架上每一部名著，每一部都是同样的序言。
classic 指末尾那一部（老师保留的那一部），是唯一有人认真读过的。
classic 意为“典范”，抽象指它承载的那条标准，父亲说 classic 就是那场考试的全部。
classic 为抽象用法，指那条标准本身，是一场考试里人人都引用、却没人质疑的东西。
classic 意为“经典作品、名著”，到 1971 年这部 classic 成了报告里的一个数字。
classic 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九百页和十一年的阅读。
classic 意为“名著”，我记得的是末尾那一部，1976 年读过，至今仍被说成全县最短的。
classic 为抽象总称，祖母说一部经典是唯一会因为被认真阅读而变好的东西。
